paragraphs.text: 1. O INDRA, drink this Soma, pressed out in the mortar, full of sweets.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्र सोममिमं पिब मधुमन्तं चमू सुतम् ।
paragraphs.translit: indra somamimaṃ piba madhumantaṃ camū sutam |

paragraphs.text: Send down to us great riches,-at your glad carouse-in thousands, O Most healthy. Thou art waxing great.
paragraphs.original: अस्मे रयिं नि धारय वि वो मदे सहस्रिणं पुरूवसो विवक्षसे
paragraphs.translit: asme rayiṃ ni dhāraya vi vo made sahasriṇaṃ purūvaso vivakṣase

paragraphs.text: 2. To thee with sacrifices, with oblations, and with lauds we come.
Lord of all strength and power, grant-at your glad carouse-the best choice worthy treasure. Thou art waxing great.
paragraphs.original: शचीपते शचीनां वि वो मदे श्रेष्ठं नो धेहि वार्यं विवक्षसे
paragraphs.translit: śacīpate śacīnāṃ vi vo made śreṣṭhaṃ no dhehi vāryaṃ vivakṣase

paragraphs.text: 3. Thou who art Lord of precious boons, inciter even of the churl.
Guardian of singers, Indra,-at your glad carouse-save us from woe and hatred. Thou art waxing great.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्र स्तोतॄणामविता वि वो मदे द्विषो नः पाह्यंहसो विवक्षसे
paragraphs.translit: indra stotṝṇāmavitā vi vo made dviṣo naḥ pāhyaṃhaso vivakṣase

paragraphs.text: 4. Strong, Lords of Magic power, ye Twain churned the united worlds apart,
When ye, implored by Vimada, Nasatyas, forced apart the pair.
5. When the united pair were rent asunder all the Gods complained.
The Gods to the Nasatyas cried, Bring these together once again.
6. Sweet be my going forth, and rich in sweets be my approach to home.
So, through your Deity, both Gods, enrich us with all pleasantness.
paragraphs.original: ता नो देवा देवतया युवं मधुमतस्कृतम्
paragraphs.translit: tā no devā devatayā yuvaṃ madhumataskṛtam
